question: How do Superfluid (CFA, GDA, Flow Councils) and Sablier (Lockup, Flow) compute balances, who holds their upgrade keys, what is their scale on 2026-10-08, and where have they failed?

frame.exposure: contract source, deployed Base contracts, subgraph and DeFiLlama reads
frame.comparator: a Tidepool member credit stream or yield-routing stream

item.title: Superfluid protocol-monorepo: ConstantFlowAgreementV1, GDA, SuperfluidPool (ethereum-contracts v1.15.3)

findings.finding: CFA stores, per account, one FlowData {timestamp, flowRate, deposit, owedDeposit}; a balance is not stored but computed: dynamicBalance = (time - state.timestamp) * state.flowRate, added to the static balance of the Super Token. Money moves with no transaction after the flow is opened.

Every flow locks a deposit sized by the governance-set liquidation period: deposit = flowRate * liquidationPeriod. A sender whose Super Token balance runs below the deposit can be liquidated by a third party (patrician period first, then pleb), so streams are collateralised by a buffer the sender must hold.

A flow is keyed by keccak256(abi.encode(flowSender, flowReceiver)) so there is one flow per ordered pair; flow-operator permissions (create/update/delete, with a flowRateAllowance) let a third contract manage a sender's flows.

GDA pools: a pool has an admin and integer member units; updateMemberUnits(member, newUnits) is described in code as mint/burn of units seen through the ERC20 lens. A distributor either distributes a lump (distribute) or sets a flow rate into the pool (distributeFlow); each member earns flowRate * units / totalUnits. Members who have not connected the pool accrue a claimable amount that claimAll settles; connected members are settled continuously.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Unit updates by admin are effectively mint/burn operations when viewed through the ERC20 lens.

findings.finding: The host, CFA and GDA are UUPS proxies (UUPSProxiable.updateCode); the governance contract that sets liquidation periods and approves agreement and Super Token logic upgrades is owned by a multisig (see the chain row).

Release ethereum-contracts@v1.15.3 and metadata@v1.6.5 were published 2026-10-01; the repo had a push on 2026-10-07; licence reported as NOASSERTION by GitHub with AGPLv3 headers in the contracts and MIT-LICENSE in ethereum-contracts.

Audit files in packages/ethereum-contracts/audits: PeckShield 2021-01, Halborn 2022-02, Trail of Bits 2023-12 (comprehensive report with fix review), "2026-01-27 Final Superfluid Collaborative Audit Report", "2026-05-25 Final Superfluid Public Best Efforts Audit Contest Report". bug-bounty.md: Immunefi; Critical USD 30,000 to 200,000, High 10,000 to 30,000, Medium 5,000, Low 2,000.

item.title: Superfluid DAO governance and tokenomics (forum thread 69) and docs governance page

findings.finding: SUP: 1 billion minted at genesis; 60 percent community (35 percent DAO treasury, 25 percent Foundation treasury) and 40 percent investors and team (about 15 and 25), unlocking one-third after a one-year cliff and the rest streaming linearly over two years. No inflation planned at the outset; DAO retains the right to mint after the initial 2 years.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: 1 billion SUP will be minted at genesis.

findings.finding: Structure: the Superfluid DAO of token holders; the Superfluid Foundation (Cayman Islands) for legal and admin support; a 3-member Security Council elected by the DAO every 6 months with emergency and non-emergency powers that the DAO can narrow or dissolve.

Voting: SIPs get a 7-day discussion, then a 14 to 16 day vote; a Constitutional SIP passes on majority with at least 5 percent of Votable Tokens voting for or abstaining and a 7-day wait; a Non-Constitutional SIP uses a 3 percent threshold, with a 3-day wait for treasury items. SUP rewards stream through Streaming Programmatic Rewards, withdrawable linearly over up to 12 months.

notFound: whether voting requires locking or staking SUP; the page does not say

findings.finding: On 2022-02-08 an attacker injected a forged ctx through callAgreement; the calldata held a real and a fake ctx, the agreement kept the first (the malicious one), and the hash check was skipped for calldata coming from the trusted Host. Halborn puts the loss at 13 million USD; REKT put the drain at 8.7 million USD.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: it kept the first version of ctx (the malicious one) and discarded the other.

notFound: Superfluid's own post-mortem text; Halborn links it but the page read did not carry it

findings.finding: Flow Council is a voting system that streams funds among recipients by weighted votes. FlowCouncil.sol keeps voters (uint96 votingPower) and recipients, with roles DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, VOTER_MANAGER_ROLE, RECIPIENT_MANAGER_ROLE; vote(Vote[]) spreads a voter's power over recipients, rejected above maxVotingSpread, and the Superfluid GDA pool units of recipients are the vote totals so the stream splits proportionally.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Flow Council is a voting system that enables organizations to dynamically stream funds among recipients based on weighted votes.

findings.finding: Factory 0x589232342bfeCb372dbbc01d17e8D112a27fF125 on Optimism, Base, Arbitrum One and Celo per the README; last push 2026-07-15. The voter set is chosen by the council admin: there is no token-weighted or identity-proof gate in the contract.

item.title: sablier-labs monorepo: lockup and flow packages

findings.finding: Lockup: a stream is an ERC-721 NFT; models are LOCKUP_LINEAR, LOCKUP_DYNAMIC, LOCKUP_TRANCHED, LOCKUP_PRICE_GATED. The full amount is deposited at creation; per-stream flags cancelable and transferable; functions withdraw, withdrawMax, cancel, renounce, burn. Streamed amount is a pure function of time and the stream parameters.

Flow: open-ended streams with no deposit up front and no end time. Stream struct {balance, ratePerSecond (UD21x18), sender, snapshotTime, isStream, isTransferable, isVoided, token, tokenDecimals, snapshotDebtScaled}; debt accrues as elapsed * ratePerSecond and is withdrawn against the balance; functions deposit, pause, refund, refundAndPause, refundMax, adjustRatePerSecond, void, withdraw; uncoveredDebtOf reports the shortfall when balance is less than debt.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: struct Stream { uint128 balance; UD21x18 ratePerSecond; address sender; uint40 snapshotTime; ... uint256 snapshotDebtScaled; }

findings.finding: Packages in the monorepo: airdrops (Merkle distribution with optional vesting), bob (price-gated vaults with optional yield adapters), flow, lockup, utils (comptroller). README: license changed from BUSL-1.1 to GPL on 2026-07-13; repository no longer maintained and not accepting pull requests, source must stay byte-for-byte verifiable against deployed addresses.

SECURITY.md: "Sablier does not operate a bug bounty program"; audits are listed in sablier-labs/audits, by Cantina and independent auditors; protocol assumptions exclude fee-on-transfer, rebasing, ERC-777 and native-wrapper tokens.
